newsitem.title: ITALY: CYCLING-'FORGOTTEN' GOTTI BUBBLES TO THE TOP.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-'FORGOTTEN' GOTTI BUBBLES TO THE TOP.

text.p: All Italy is talking about new hero Ivan Gotti, who three weeks ago was the forgotten man of the Giro d'Italia.
"No one took me seriously," he said after starting a nine-day reign in the leader's pink jersey of the Giro which he won on Sunday.
A cat crossing the street came as a catastrophe for Italy in the second week of the race, sending Italian dreams plummeting with the luckless Marco Pantani.
"It was said the Giro was finished for Italy when Marco was injured in that crash," Gotti said.
With their main hope taken out by a tabby on a mountain descent, the tifosi (fans) mourned even though Gotti lay third overall.
His mission was to restore their faith.
He had felt slighted at the Venice start because he was not invited to the pre-Giro press conference with other contenders.
Instead they called on his colourful teammate Mario Cipollini whose turn of phrase is as fast as his finish.
Yet Gotti was fifth last year when his big rival and friend, Russian Pavel Tonkov, won the Giro.
Gotti had also worn the yellow jersey of Tour de France leader for two days in 1995, and was fifth in the 1996 Tour.
Though after five years as a professional he could boast only one success when he won a Giro stage last year in the Dolomites. His second came on the Breuil Cervinia mountain nine days ago.

He could not wait to escape the shadow of his more respected teammates in the early years, first Gianni Bugno, a former world champion and Giro winner, then Russian Yevgeny Berzin, who won the 1994 Giro.
"I wanted a team where I could be a leader," said Gotti.
With the success came the pressure.
"Psychologically, I suffered in my new role as Giro leader, what with the television, press and the public," said Gotti, who will have even more stress next month in the Tour de France.
The Giro has been tough also for mamma and papa Gotti in front of their TV in the spa town of San Pellegrino, noted for its bubbling water.
"It has been a week of praying and lighting candles, and suffering," said father Gino. "I have lost weight because I could not eat. Now I am in paradise."
Brother Ugo and the town band will strike up at the Milan finish, and all week Ugo has been practising the Triumphal March from Aida on his clarinet.
Then the party begins, and they will be toasting their hero with a different bubbly to that which, before Gotti, put San Pellegrino on the map.
